values.binNote: The bin only stores the total bleed damage (NaafiriQ.BleedBaseDamage=[35/60/85/110/135], bonus AD ratio 0.8) delivered over BleedDuration=5 seconds in ticks every BleedInterval=0.5s, i.e. 10 ticks. The wiki's per-tick value divides these totals by 10 (35/10..135/10, 0.8/10=0.08); no bin row states the per-tick number directly.

TotalMaxDamageSecondCast = (BaseDamageSecondCast + SecondCastMaxADRatio=0.7 x bonus ad) * ExecuteMultiplier=2, which yields base 2x[30/42.5/55/67.5/80]=[60/85/110/135/160] and AD coefficient 0.7*2=1.4, matching the wiki numbers; ExecuteMultiplier and SecondCastMaxADRatio are only multiplicative factors within that calculation and carry no standalone number stated by this value.

primitives.note: Packmates spawn passively up to a level-gated cap (present at max from fight start per P), W temporarily adds 2 more, and R has each active Packmate land its own smaller collision-damage instance on the target.
Darkin Daggers applies a bleed dealing bonus physical damage in ticks every 0.5s over 5s.

Q has a free recast within a window that behaves differently depending on target bleed state; E's dash-hit and arrival flurry are two separately timed damage instances; R has a conditional free recast after a takedown.
Q's recast bonus damage on an already-bleeding target scales with the target's missing health (base +0-100%, scaling +0-250%), capped at 100% missing health.
The Call of the Pack grants 20% bonus AD and bonus movement speed for the 5s hunt duration, which feeds into bonus-AD ratios on Q/E/R cast during it.
We Are More's summon cooldown is reduced 4s per champion/large-monster ability hit and 1s per kill; R grants a free recast within 12s if a takedown occurs within 7s of cast.
Mana costs (Q 50-90, W 60, E 40, R 100) can gate how many casts fit in the 15s window depending on mana pool/regen.
Hounds' Pursuit channels for 0.75s (blocking other actions) before the dash and damage resolve.

needsBespoke.why: The kit's damage-relevant pieces (bleed dot, recast burst with missing-health scaling, timed AD buff, Packmate pet damage, channel-then-dash burst, cooldown refunds) all map onto existing primitives. The main open work is picking concrete assumptions (Packmate count present, whether the fight ever produces a takedown, exact recast timing) rather than needing new mechanics.

proposal: Start the fight with the level-appropriate cap of Packmates already active (per We Are More's passive) fighting alongside Naafiri.
Open with The Call of the Pack (W) to gain 20% bonus AD and the hunt buff before committing to other casts, so subsequent AD-scaling abilities hit harder.
Follow immediately with Hounds' Pursuit (R): channel 0.75s, then dash in and deal the collision damage plus each active Packmate's smaller collision hit; this also extends W's hunt duration by 1.75s.
Cast Eviscerate (E) at the target's location for the dash-through damage plus the arrival flurry damage.
Cast Darkin Daggers (Q) for the initial hit and bleed application, then recast Q as soon as the recast lockout elapses (within the 4s free-recast window) to land the bleeding-target bonus damage.
Auto-attack with Naafiri and Packmates on cooldown/attack timer between ability casts.
Re-cast Q, E, W, and R on cooldown for the remainder of the 15s window in whichever order clears cooldowns fastest, prioritizing keeping W's AD buff active as much as possible.
Do not expect a free R recast from a takedown, since the dummy does not die mid-fight (unless the fight is defined to end in a kill).
questions: Is the simulator expected to model Naafiri's Packmates as independently attacking pets with their own attack-speed timers, or approximate their contribution as a flat periodic damage add-on?
When W's bonus AD buff is active for only part of the fight, does the simulator recompute AD-scaling ability damage per-cast using AD at cast time, or use a single average AD across the whole fight?

Should the optimal Q usage be back-to-back casts (burst the bleeding-target bonus quickly) or spacing casts so the bleed fully resolves before a fresh Q application, given the unsettled question about what recasting on a bleeding target actually does to total damage?
Does R's 0.75s channel fully block Naafiri's other actions (no auto-attacks, no other casts) during that window, reducing the total number of casts achievable in 15s?
